# Unified QA Automation Platform — Master Contract

Authority: supplied Development Plan v2, Multi-Harness Edition. Status: architecture approved; development readiness unverified. Active authorization is recorded in harness/state.json and must match explicit user/operator approval. This architectural contract grants no phase or step authorization.

## Architecture and boundaries
Exactly five independent product repositories: qa-features, sut-python, sut-node, qa-python, qa-typescript. Use sibling directories; the workspace is not a Git repository. Create repositories only in their authorized step. No sixth governance repository. Preserve the tested canonical harness in qa-features as separate governance artifacts once Step 1 permits its creation; propagate generated native adapters to later repositories. Clean checkouts must work without untracked parent files.

## Frozen contracts
Use Conduit authentication and `Authorization: Token <jwt>`. Maintain one synthetic immutable baseline user and unique generated registration identities. UI selectors use only role, label, or data-testid. Preserve original story and AC tags. AC-3 requires UI error, no browser session, and protected-route denial. Independently check unauthenticated GET /user returns 401 with Hurl.
Observer states: complete, partial, unavailable, error. Six matrix slots, three scenarios each. One report per issue/campaign. No runtime model calls, auto-healing, or silent test changes to accommodate defects in QA CI.
Runners pin qa-features with feature_ref; reporting may separately pin tooling_ref. Relative GitHub submodule URL: ../qa-features.git. Local file transport requires explicit trusted-workstation authorization.

## Authorization gates
Phase 0: readiness. Phase 0.5A: shared harness; 0.5B: native adapters; 0.5C: skills/evaluation. Each requires its own authorized scope. Stop after Phase 0.5 pending explicit Step 1 authorization. No step implicitly authorizes another.
Step 1 produces a validated, untagged specification. Human approval separately permits an immutable feature tag. Agents cannot self-approve or autonomously tag. Steps 2–7 require explicit individual authorization and prerequisites. See planning/development-plan.md.

## Harness obligations
One authoritative shared controller, three adapters: Antigravity, Codex, Claude Code. Native artifacts must be verified against each provider's actual supported protocol. Never assume equivalent hooks or blocking semantics. Codex command rules are not a universal filesystem sandbox.
Use provider permissions, supported interception, preflight, filesystem/Git auditing, and human approval together. Final deterministic scope auditing is mandatory. Maintain schema-validated state and evidence separately from QA results/campaign schemas. Explicit human authorization must have external provenance; agent-edited state is not approval.
Only one writable owner per step. Release ownership before transfer. Receiving agents inspect state, handoff, and Git status and run preflight. Read-only independent reviews are allowed; concurrent writable agents are prohibited.
Four canonical skills: qa-step-executor, qa-contract-author, qa-verification, qa-architecture-reviewer. Canonical source is .agents/skills; Claude copies are deterministically generated and checked for drift. Native discovery must be tested from each repository's working directory.

## Security and integrity
No production secrets, blanket unrestricted shell permissions, unauthorized dependencies, unreviewed changes to approved features, automatic weakening of acceptance criteria, or future-step scaffolding. QA CI remains deterministic and separate from the development harness. Successful command execution alone is not acceptance evidence. Missing instrumentation cannot produce PASS.
Every implementation response includes summary, file tree, exact commands, PASS/FAIL/NOT RUN checklist, blockers/approvals, remaining unbuilt work, and an explicit boundary stop.
Release preserves image digests and provenance for application configuration and development harness. Preserve reporting integrity and rollback/reproduction evidence.

The user explicitly stated: “I dont have claude access, lets just create the file for them”. Retain and statically validate all Claude native instructions, settings, hooks and mirrored skills. Defer live Claude discovery, enforcement and handoff testing; those checks remain NOT RUN. The current Phase 0.5 exit gate requires live Antigravity → Codex → Antigravity validation and Claude artifact validation. This exception supersedes only the earlier all-three-live readiness requirement. It does not waive Step 1 inputs, step prerequisites, feature approval or product boundaries. Claude cannot claim writable ownership under the artifacts-only profile; validate and reactivate the stricter all-live profile before using it as a writer. The approval receipt is harness/approved-exceptions.json; executable policy is harness/config/providers.yaml.
# Development harness

This controller governs coding agents. It is never imported by pytest-bdd/Cypress or run in deterministic QA CI. Active work is Phase 0.5 completion; Step 1 has already been requested but awaits its other prerequisites. No product repositories exist. See MASTER-CONTRACT.md for architectural authority.

## Bootstrap and verify

Use Python 3.11+ (tested on 3.14.4). From the workspace root:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r harness/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python harness/scripts/sync_skills.py --check
.venv/bin/python harness/scripts/preflight.py --step 0.5 --provider codex --owner phase05-builder
.venv/bin/python harness/scripts/validate_adapters.py
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s harness/evals -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

JSON-compatible YAML configuration deliberately uses the YAML JSON subset. PyYAML parses it; schemas use JSON Schema 2020-12. Dependencies are isolated, pinned, and unrelated to future runner environments.

Before implementation retain an external protected filesystem baseline; `scope_guard.py --baseline <path> --capture` refuses overwrite. For this preparation run the retained baseline is harness/evidence/baseline.json plus the Phase 0 workspace manifest. Final auditing uses `scope_guard.py --baseline harness/evidence/baseline.json`. Baseline loss is a blocker, never permission to silently reset it.

## Evidence and gates

The operator provisions an external random recorder key of at least 32 bytes, mode 0600, and sets QA_EVIDENCE_KEY_FILE. This run stores its key in the sibling qa-workspace-control directory; never commit it or print its contents. Evidence records execution, source fingerprint, logs and HMAC. Key holders can sign evidence: this detects edited/fabricated records without the key, not malicious actions by the trusted recorder itself. Independently protect the baseline, ledger and recorder key with OS permissions and human review. Same-user agents cannot be sandboxed by their own editable scripts alone.

.venv/bin/python harness/scripts/verify_step.py gate

## Ownership and approvals

Read-only inspection is permitted without claiming writable ownership. To switch writers, use `ownership.py release --provider <old> --owner <id> --handoff harness/evidence/handoff.json`, then `ownership.py claim --provider <new> --owner <id> --handoff harness/evidence/handoff.json`. Receiving owner inspects the handoff and Git state, then runs preflight. The transfer is serialized with a file lock and refuses unreleased ownership or changed handoff state. No parallel writers.

For a product step, a human must maintain an external QA_AUTHORIZATION_FILE with step, source=human, reference, and approved_feature_ref, matching the persisted authorization. The controller does not create it. State edits alone cannot grant product access. The external file and state are administrative inputs, not an identity/authentication service; protect them externally. Feature/tooling refs must resolve to recorded immutable commits when set. Feature tagging remains human controlled. Missing Phase 0 prerequisites and prior contracts block Step 1.

## Provider controls and gaps

Antigravity uses .agents/hooks.json with named hook groups, native camelCase payloads and decision=deny; PostToolUse returns empty JSON, so audit findings are persisted for external review. Rules use trigger=always_on. A stdlib-only launcher reads workspacePaths from the native payload and invokes the absolute project interpreter/script path; it does not assume the hook working directory. Live verification must confirm this for each surface.

Claude uses .claude/settings.json, snake_case tool fields and hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision. CLAUDE.md contains only @AGENTS.md; documented import handling avoids duplicate loading. A user's managed-only instructions or disabled hooks can bypass project customizations; live verification remains mandatory. Stop hooks report blockers without creating infinite continuation loops.

Codex uses project sandbox/approval defaults and execpolicy rules. No custom Codex lifecycle hooks are configured. Trusted project activation is required; scope enforcement relies on OS sandbox and explicit preflight/audit, not command rules as a filesystem sandbox. Native probes use a temporary command-line trust setting, never edit personal trust configuration or select a model.

File-tool actions are checked before writes where supported. Unknown tools are denied. Claude shell effects require scoped human permission; Antigravity shell calls are denied pending external scoped execution because headless ask semantics were not reliable in the live probe. Shell text is not treated as a safe filesystem proof. Final auditing checks tracked/untracked paths, empty directories, symlinks and Git references. Non-root .venv directories are included. .git internals, Python caches and the root isolated environment require provider permissions; they are excluded from content hashing. Evidence permits only report/log/JSON/lock artifacts and validates recorder records separately. Audit cannot detect transient writes that were reverted, changes outside inspected workspaces, or files hidden in excluded runtime directories; native sandboxing and independent review cover these gaps.

## Provenance and clean checkout

Before Step 1, source is this non-Git workspace. Export with package_governance.py --output <new-tar-path> to retain a reproducible source bundle and file hashes. Use --repository <authorized-repository-name> when generating a repository-local bundle; location metadata maps local paths to the central step policy and requires an independent Git root. It creates no repository itself. On Step 1 preserve the canonical source under qa-features governance separately from business contracts. Later authorized repositories receive generated native artifacts plus self-contained shared scripts/contracts and a provenance manifest. Do not depend on parent untracked files or cross-repository symlinks. Distribution initializes state with no authorization or writable owner; an operator supplies local authorization. Clean-room export tests run in disposable fixtures without creating actual product repositories. Native discovery from each real repository remains an acceptance check when it is created.

The native cycle uses a temporary Codex home and --trust only for its disposable fixture, with a temporary login-file link. It never saves trust or configuration in the personal Codex home, copies credentials into governance, or disables the read-only sandbox. Model responses alone cannot establish enforcement: actual tool-denial diagnostics/events and unchanged files are required. Legacy live_probe.py remains a partial diagnostic, not the completion check.
